intro_md: 🎧 **9 min. New listening – not the article.** It's Saturday morning in the café. Sam started a new habit two months ago. Listen first; the words are hidden.

parts.title: Sam's new habit
parts.md:
![Sam walks to work](data/img/w1/d14-sam-walk.webp)

**Two small phrases – same words, different jobs:**

- **used to + verb** = a habit in the past that has stopped. 👉 *My dad **used to smoke**, but he stopped.* (He doesn't smoke now.) Sounds like **"yoostə"**.
- **be used to + -ing** = it's normal for you now, so it isn't hard. 👉 *I'm **used to getting up** early.* (It was hard before. Now it's easy.)

💡 Quick test: is there a verb with **-ing** after *to*? Then it's *be used to* – "normal now". Listen for both in the chat.

**Train your ears – the words are hidden at first:**
1. 👂 **Listen without the words.** Just follow. Missed a word? Keep going – the next sentence often explains it.
2. 👂 **Listen again**, still without the words. You'll catch more.
3. 📄 **Show transcript** – listen + read. **Tap any line** you missed to hear just that part again.
4. 👂 **Hide it** and listen one last time.

listen.text: Morning, Sam. You look very awake for a Saturday.
I've just walked here. It's about forty minutes from my flat.
Forty minutes? You used to take the bus, didn't you?
I did, but two months ago I decided to try walking to work.
The bus was always full, and I arrived at the office already annoyed.
Now I'm in a better mood before I even sit down at my desk.
Much better, actually. I fall asleep in ten minutes now.
And I get my best ideas on the way. Yesterday I solved a problem in the park.
That's interesting. What about the money?
I save about forty pounds a month, so that's nice.
And the rain? This is Manchester, after all.
That's the only problem. I'm used to walking in the rain now, but my shoes aren't.
I used to cycle every day, but I stopped after I hurt my knee.
Why don't you walk with me one morning?
Maybe. I'll bring a bigger umbrella.

parts.title: Quick check + how was it?
parts.md: A few quick questions – tap an answer, you see right away if it's right. Then tell me how much you understood, ask me anything below, and 📤 **Submit**.

questions.q: Why did Sam stop taking the bus?

check.why: Sam says: *The bus was always full, and I arrived at the office already annoyed.*

questions.q: What is the only problem with walking?

check.why: Sam says: *That's the only problem* – she is used to the rain, but her shoes aren't.

questions.q: How much did you understand? Write a number, e.g. 80
